effect_mechanism: Water held by runoff structures supports plant growth and habitat around them: the WOCAT compiler for gabions and rock check dams in Somalia reports that improved soil moisture and reduced erosion supported the growth of different plant and grass species, and that the restored vegetation and water created better conditions for livestock and small wildlife [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_animal_diversity]. Users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive greener surroundings and improved biodiversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_veno12_1]. Embrapa reports that crops, vegetable gardens and orchards on the humid fringes of its barraginhas in Brazil bring back fauna that had disappeared for lack of food [ev_biodiversity_outcome_mira19_3].
conditionality: The gain is slight: the compiler units all come from a single Somali technology sheet and are mostly rated as slight change, the Ghana unit is a user perception, and no unit measures species or habitat [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_veno12_1]. The Brazilian barraginha fauna finding is an adopter-reported indicator in Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no species measured [ev_biodiversity_outcome_mira19_3].

effect_mechanism: In semi-arid settings the practices add carbon removals mainly through soil storage: organic matter concentrated in zaï pits raised soil organic matter content from 1 to 1.4 percent on soils treated 3 and 5 years earlier in Burkina Faso, and farms using zaï and/or rock bunds there had more soil carbon than a control farm [ev_soil_organic_carbon_kabo04_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3]. Check dams on China's Loess Plateau store carbon in the sediment trapped behind them, and that storage increases with time at both check dam and watershed levels [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1].
conditionality: The gain is rated slight because no unit states how large the carbon removal is per hectare or per year: the zaï figure is an organic-matter content change cited second-hand from an earlier study, the Burkina Faso farm comparison is a soil-fertility test against a single control farm, and the Loess Plateau statement is a review citation [ev_soil_organic_carbon_kabo04_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3, ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1]. Soil organic matter and trapped sediment stand in for a measured carbon stock change, and carbon in check-dam sediment partly moves carbon eroded from upslope rather than removing new carbon from the air.

effect_mechanism: Carbon removal here is soil storage, plus carbon held in trapped sediment: a review of infiltration trenches reports that trenches combined with vegetation raised soil nutrients including soil organic carbon [ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_1]. A check-dam review cites check dams on China's Loess Plateau contributing to carbon sequestration, an effect that grows with time at both dam and watershed level as sediment accumulates [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1]. A meta-analysis of Chinese soil and water conservation measures, available as a preprint, finds soil organic carbon 10.74% to 22.63% above the initial level after straw mulching across regions, and 3.36% and 75.77% higher after contour tillage in two regions within 5 to 10 years [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_3, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_4]. The same preprint meta-analysis finds terracing raised soil organic carbon by 27%, 17.94% and 26.62% in three Chinese regions, with increases of 14.11% to 60.96% in regional subsets 11 to 30 years after construction [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_5, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_6, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_7, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_8, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_9, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_10, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_11]. A Chinese meta-analysis, available as a preprint, reports fish-scale pits raising soil organic carbon storage by 79.86% on the Loess Plateau in years 11~30 [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_12].
conditionality: The trench review also reports that trenches in Mexico actually decreased soil nitrogen and carbon, so the trench evidence is split [ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_2]. Soil organic carbon gains stand in for carbon removal; none of the units reports a net greenhouse-gas balance. The Loess Plateau check-dam result is a secondary citation without a magnitude in the quoted passage [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1]. The Chinese figures come from a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, in an upper-middle-income country. Several are the values for the duration window with the greatest increase rather than a pooled estimate, and the duration subsets overlap the regional ones [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_3, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_8, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_12]. In this scope the preprint carries most of the measured signal.

effect_mechanism: In-field practices store carbon in the soil as organic matter builds up where water and organic inputs are held: zai fields in Burkina Faso treated for several years had higher organic matter and trenches combined with vegetation raised soil organic carbon [ev_soil_organic_carbon_kabo04_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_1]. A meta-analysis of Chinese soil and water conservation measures, available as a preprint, finds soil organic carbon 10.74% to 22.63% above the initial level after straw mulching across regions, and 3.36% and 75.77% higher after contour tillage in two regions within 5 to 10 years [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_3, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_4].
conditionality: The evidence is mixed: trenches in Mexico reduced soil nitrogen and carbon, and a zai trial in Burkina Faso detected no significant change in organic matter even though biomass production rose [ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_roose93_1]. The size of the gain rests on the Chinese figures, which come from a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, in an upper-middle-income country, and cover straw mulching and contour tillage rather than pits or trenches; the contour-tillage values are for the 5-to-10-year window with the greatest increase, not a pooled estimate [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_3, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_4]. Paired soil samples from Zambian fields under planting basins or ripping (bundled with reduced tillage), with crop residues hardly retained, showed no significant difference in organic carbon from conventional fields [ev_soil_organic_carbon_umar11_4].

effect_mechanism: Carbon removal here runs through vegetation and soil: WOCAT compilers judge that gabions and rock check dams in Somalia increase above-ground biomass and soil organic matter through vegetation recovery and sediment accumulation, storing more carbon in plants and soils, and a second Somali sheet reports some soil organic matter gain as vegetation and soil cover regenerate [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7778_2026_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7778_2026_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7778_2026_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7777_2026_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C]. A check-dam review cites check dams on China's Loess Plateau contributing to carbon sequestration, an effect that grows with time at both dam and watershed level as sediment accumulates [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1].
conditionality: Apart from the Loess Plateau check-dam finding, which is a secondary citation in a review with no magnitude in the quoted passage, all units are practitioner judgements from Somali technology sheets, all rated slight, with no measured carbon; biomass, soil organic matter and avoided-emission ratings are proxies for carbon removal, and most units come from the same Somali sheet [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7778_2026_biomass_above_ground_C].

effect_mechanism: Terraces store carbon in the soil: a preprint meta-analysis of Chinese soil and water conservation measures finds terracing raised soil organic carbon by 27%, 17.94% and 26.62% in three Chinese regions, with increases of 14.11% to 60.96% in regional subsets 11 to 30 years after construction [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_5, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_6, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_7, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_8, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_9, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_10, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_11]. The compiler for gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan expects the expanding root system to increase below-ground soil organic matter and carbon [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7553_2025_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C].
conditionality: The preprint sets the strength of this row: it has not been peer reviewed, it is from an upper-middle-income country, and its duration figures are the windows with obvious increases, overlapping the regional estimates [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_8, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_10]. The WOCAT units are practitioner ratings, not measured carbon stocks; the Bhutan stone-bund sheet says organic matter falls at the upper part of the terrace and rises at the lower part, a redistribution within the field rather than a net removal [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_6891_2023_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7553_2025_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C].

effect_mechanism: In the Sahel, stone bunds, zaï and half-moons applied at watershed scale increase ground water level [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1], and in Burkina Faso levels of water in wells have improved, which the source links not to higher rainfall but to SWC measures that control surface runoff and improve infiltration [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1]. On China's Loess Plateau, a large campaign of check-dam construction carried out since the 1970s to retain floodwater and intercept soil sediments reduced streamflow by approximately 39% [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]. In Burkina Faso, cited studies show soil and water conservation techniques improving the availability of ground water in many villages, especially large rock bunds known as digues filtrantes [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6].
conditionality: Both sides are real findings in semi-arid land, and what separates them is the outcome measured, the place and the scale of the works. The gain is groundwater and well levels on and around treated Sahelian fields and watersheds [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1]; the loss is streamflow below a campaign of check dams built at very large scale in China to retain floodwater [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]. For a downstream user the Chinese finding is the relevant one; for a farmer near the works the Sahelian one is. Neither side compares with and without the works at catchment scale: the Sahelian units are cited statements, the 39% is cited by a review from another study, and in Burkina Faso the number of wells with water year round has not increased significantly since SWC began [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2]. A further Burkina Faso statement, cited from another study with no figures, also sits on the gain side [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6].

effect_mechanism: Upstream capture can both add to and take from downstream water. On China's Loess Plateau, a large campaign of check-dam construction carried out since the 1970s to retain floodwater and intercept soil sediments reduced streamflow by approximately 39% [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]. On the other side, Embrapa says its barraginhas in Brazil help recharge groundwater by raising the water table and revitalise springs and rivers [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6], and in the Peruvian Andes a few studies have observed catchment-level changes such as reduced quick runoff or increased aquifer recharge, which the source calls plausible but not generalisable [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1].
conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks what capturing water upstream does to the water that reaches streams and reservoirs below, not whether the farm that captures it has more. The sides now conflict, and what separates them is what is measured and at what scale: the loss is streamflow below a check-dam campaign at very large scale built to retain floodwater [ev_water_yield_luca21_1], while the gains are recharge and water-table statements for small dispersed basins and trenches [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1]. In the Peruvian Andes trenches had little effect on increasing baseflow, with hydrogeological characteristics key to explaining their impact [ev_water_regulation_locat20_1]. None of this is a measured project comparison: the 39% is a secondary citation in a global review, the Peruvian statements are a review's summary, and the barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology [ev_water_yield_luca21_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6].

effect_mechanism: In the Maghreb, mechanised bund systems, built with large machines that scrape a 4 to 10 m strip to raise bunds 1.5 to 2 m high every 30 to 50 m, considerably reduce the water collected in downstream hill reservoirs and cost 10 to 25% of the cultivable area [ev_water_yield_roos10_1]. On the other side, earth and stone bunds in Mauritania were built to facilitate water infiltration and replenish groundwater tables, and surveyed communities expressed satisfaction with the rising levels of water in their wells [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mrt14_1]; in the Peruvian Andes a few studies have observed catchment-level changes such as increased aquifer recharge, which the source calls plausible but not generalisable [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1].
conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks what capturing water upstream does to the water that reaches streams and reservoirs below, not whether the farm that captures it has more. The sides are measured in different places: the gains are well levels and recharge around the treated land, the loss is water reaching downstream hill reservoirs below mechanised bunds, and a downstream loss can coexist with the local gain. The source ties the loss to mechanised construction and cites it from earlier work in an expert manual; the Mauritanian gain is a lender-reported community perception for works that also included fencing [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mrt14_1]; and in the Peruvian Andes trenches had little effect on increasing baseflow, with hydrogeological characteristics key to explaining their impact [ev_water_regulation_locat20_1]. No finding is quantified.

The Cameroonian source flags that the drainage could reach the unterraced piedmonts, a much more fragile environment [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1]. On-slope supply evidence for terraces is in the terracing water stress row.

effect_mechanism: Terraces, contour stone bunds, check dams and small dams slow and spread runoff and retain water and sediment, lowering peak discharges: terraces lowered flood peaks on small mountain plots, stone bunds lower peak discharges at the foot of the slope, and in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment a combined treatment cut the runoff volume of 71 single-peak floods by 50% [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s]. WOCAT compilers in Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, Tunisia and Uzbekistan rate flooding as reduced and say how: rain retained where it falls, a dam or series of dams acting as a downstream buffer, stone lines and walls cutting peak flows, and structures slowing runoff velocity [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_flood_impacts]. Users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive fewer rainy-season floods, spate and diversion structures in Yemen are said to control floods, and compacted hill terraces in Uttarakhand, India are credited with limiting flood and landslide damage [ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7]. A check-dam review cites check dams mitigating flooding and significantly reducing peak flow in Iran and check-dam sequences proving effective against strong floods in Italian torrents, and small hill dams in Morocco are credited with damping damage in the serious 2002-2003 floods [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1]. Embrapa credits its barraginhas, small runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths in Brazil, with easing floods as well [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].
conditionality: The sub-practices disagree, and the split runs through terracing: bunds and terraces that slow and spread runoff on the slope lowered peak discharges, while structures that divert runoff did the opposite — diversion banquettes in Niger raised peak discharges and runoff-diversion systems accelerate concentration time [ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3]. Runoff-catchment and spate rows each show a moderate benefit on their own, so whether the practice eases or worsens flood hazard depends on whether it holds water in place or concentrates it. Size and extremes matter too: larger sand dams increase flooding risk, and check dams have a minimal effect against extreme floods, especially where ill-designed or poorly maintained [ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_3]. Catchment-scale measurement is scarce, with a review calling the terrace effect on peak flow uncertain; the Tunisian result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds, the Yemen and Uttarakhand statements are lender self-reported, the review's supporting cases are secondary citations, and the Italian ones are mountain torrent control in a high-income setting [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2]. The barraginha flood statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, unmeasured, and a landscape-scale effect rather than one on the adopting farm [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].

effect_mechanism: Dams, check dams and gabions slow runoff and buffer peak flows: WOCAT compilers in Kenya, Ethiopia and Somalia rate flooding as reduced, the Kenyan sheet because a dam or series of dams creates a buffer downstream, the Ethiopian because the structure and rehabilitated areas reduce the speed of the flood, and the Somali because stone lines, gabions and rock check dams reduced runoff velocity; users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive fewer rainy-season floods [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1]. A check-dam review cites check dams mitigating flooding and significantly reducing peak flow in Iran and check-dam sequences proving effective against strong floods in Italian torrents, and small hill dams in Morocco are credited with damping damage in the serious 2002-2003 floods [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1]. Embrapa credits its barraginhas, small runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths in Brazil, with easing floods as well [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].
conditionality: Nearly all units are practitioner judgements, user perceptions or secondary citations, not measurements. Size can reverse the effect: a review notes larger sand dams raise flooding, erosion and seepage risk [ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1]. The check-dam review finds a minimal effect against extreme floods, especially where structures are ill-designed or poorly maintained; its supporting cases are secondary citations, and the Italian ones are mountain torrent control in a high-income setting [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_3, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2]. The barraginha flood statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, unmeasured, and a landscape-scale effect rather than one on the adopting farm [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].

effect_mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces, stone lines and contour stone bunds detain and spread runoff on slopes, lowering peak discharges and making flows last longer after rain; in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment a combined treatment cut the runoff volume of 71 single-peak floods by 50% [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s], and WOCAT compilers in Tunisia and Uzbekistan judge flooding reduced, the Tunisian stone-lines sheet citing lower peak flows during heavy rainfall [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_flood_impacts].
conditionality: The studies disagree because they cover different structures: diversion banquettes in Niger raised peak discharges, and runoff-diversion dikes speed up concentration time and risk gullying if they break, so design decides the sign [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3]. effect_mechanism: Harvested water and held soil moisture raise harvests and diversify diets: in semi-arid Kenya planting basins (zai pits) raised the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement to 421.75 against 1.67 in the control, bunds improve household food security in proportion to the farm area they cover, and Burkina Faso farms applying manure or soil and water conservation techniques on over half their plots are cited as more food secure [ev_food_security_boil19_2, ev_food_security_zoug14_1, ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5]. In semi-arid Brazil stored production water allows daily irrigation of vegetable gardens and fruit trees for families who previously did not grow or eat vegetables, subsurface dams gave families more access to fruit and vegetables and more food overall, reviews of production-cistern experiments stress their importance for food security, and a systematic review cites significant improvements in food security indicators among adopters of rainwater-harvesting ponds in Burkina Faso [ev_food_security_arsky20_6, ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_food_security_castro22_3, ev_food_security_silv26_1].
conditionality: The gain depends on rain: Niger farm families with soil and water conservation produced an estimated surplus of 70 percent in years of good rainfall but still had an estimated deficit of 28 percent in low-rainfall years, so the practice does not secure food in dry years [ev_food_security_kabo04_1]. The only sized result is the Kenyan odds ratio, which has a wide confidence interval and comes from an above-average rainfall season [ev_food_security_boil19_2]. The Brazilian units are implementer perceptions, a seven-family interview study and a review of experiments run by the technology's developer, the Burkina Faso farm statement bundles manure with the conservation works, and the systematic review's citation is contradicted by its own table [ev_food_security_arsky20_6, ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_food_security_castro22_3, ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5, ev_food_security_silv26_1].

effect_mechanism: In upper-middle-income semi-arid Brazil, stored water lets families grow food close to home: once production water is stored it allows daily irrigation of gardens, beds and fruit trees, and most families had not even been in the habit of growing and eating vegetables before [ev_food_security_arsky20_6]. Families with subsurface dams gained more varied diets, mainly through more access to fruit and vegetables, and most of those interviewed reported more food available [ev_food_security_cirilo03_6]; a review of Embrapa experiments judges irrigation of small beds from production cisterns important for household food security [ev_food_security_castro22_3], and adopters of barraginha runoff basins identified food security, in quantity, quality and diversity, as the technology's greatest impact [ev_food_security_mira19_2].
conditionality: The gain is rated slight because no unit gives a size of effect: the evidence is qualitative interviews, an expert account of a cistern programme, a review of the research institute's own experiments, and an adopter-rated indicator in Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology [ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_food_security_arsky20_6, ev_food_security_castro22_3, ev_food_security_mira19_2]. All of it comes from semi-arid Brazil and works through garden irrigation and diet diversity rather than staple-crop supply, so it describes household storage for home production, not field-scale harvesting.

effect_mechanism: Across mixed soil and water conservation and water-harvesting programmes, the reported route to lower food insecurity is higher yields and irrigated gardens. A review tabulates significantly increased food security from check dams and infiltration pits in Malawi [ev_food_security_ngur26_1]; Brazilian studies judge production-cistern irrigation of small beds feasible and important for household food security [ev_food_security_castro22_3]; and higher yields are cited as improving food security in Burkina Faso, especially on farms with soil and water conservation on over half of their plots [ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5].
conditionality: The gain is only slight because the supporting findings are qualitative, cited second-hand and give no size, while the independent evaluations point the other way. In Ethiopia, an impact evaluation of a bundled watershed project found no significant food-security effect for treated households at any participation level [ev_food_security_abate21_4], and public-works participation in communal soil and water investments did not translate into increased food security, possibly because of the short programme [ev_food_security_arega24_1]; both concern mostly off-farm community works. In Niger, families with soil and water conservation produced a surplus of 70 percent in good rainfall years but a deficit of 28 percent in low-rainfall years [ev_food_security_kabo04_1], so benefits may not hold in the dry years that matter most.

effect_mechanism: Planting basins and ground cover hold rain where crops grow, raising staple harvests. Planting basins (zai pits) raised the odds of a Kenyan plot meeting the household maize requirement to 421.75 against 1.67 in the control, and ground cover raised those odds in Malawi's El Nino season [ev_food_security_boil19_2, ev_food_security_boil19_1].
conditionality: Practice choice and season matter. In the same Malawian El Nino season, banking lowered the odds of meeting the maize requirement from 0.19 to 0.054, so a mis-matched in-field practice can deepen food shortfall [ev_food_security_boil19_3]. The large Kenyan odds come from an above-average rainfall season and do not show performance in drought [ev_food_security_boil19_2]. Every unit comes from the same study, a plot-level analysis of yield thresholds rather than a household food-security survey, which is why the strong class stands on a narrow base.

justification.mechanism: Planting basins and ground cover hold rain where crops grow, raising staple harvests. Planting basins (zai pits) raised the odds of a Kenyan plot meeting the household maize requirement to 421.75 against 1.67 in the control, and ground cover raised those odds in Malawi's El Nino season [ev_food_security_boil19_2, ev_food_security_boil19_1].
justification.conditionality: Practice choice and season matter. In the same Malawian El Nino season, banking lowered the odds of meeting the maize requirement from 0.19 to 0.054, so a mis-matched in-field practice can deepen food shortfall [ev_food_security_boil19_3]. The large Kenyan odds come from an above-average rainfall season and do not show performance in drought [ev_food_security_boil19_2]. Every unit comes from the same study, a plot-level analysis of yield thresholds rather than a household food-security survey, which is why the strong class stands on a narrow base.

effect_mechanism: Vallerani tractor-ploughed micro-catchments collect runoff for fodder and crops. conditionality: This cell is data deficient, not a finding of no effect: both units come from a single WOCAT technology sheet for Burkina Faso and are practitioner ratings, and no study measures household food security for micro-catchment practices. effect_mechanism: Water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia, spate irrigation in Eritrea and marab floodplain farming in Jordan divert and spread floodwater over fields: the Ethiopian compiler states it is the expert's conviction that crop production increased with water harvested and spread over the farm as spate or supplementary irrigation to the seasonal rainfall [ev_crop_yield_wocat_6715_2023_crop_production]. Much of the gain goes to livestock: in Jordan the barley is mostly used to feed animals and the stubble is grazed, in Eritrea residues are fed to livestock, and in Ethiopia fodder rises with the soil and moisture conserved behind the structure, with animal production increasing as feed becomes more available [ev_forage_productivity_wocat_5770_2020_fodder_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1333_2010_fodder_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_6715_2023_fodder_production, ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_6715_2023_animal_production].
conditionality: Every unit is a practitioner rating from a WOCAT technology sheet; there is no literature measurement in this cell, and the Ethiopian crop rating is stated as the expert's conviction rather than a yield comparison [ev_crop_yield_wocat_6715_2023_crop_production]. Most of the remaining support is for fodder and animal production rather than food crops, which is why the class is only slight [ev_forage_productivity_wocat_5770_2020_fodder_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1333_2010_fodder_production].

effect_mechanism: In the Maghreb, contour structures have been reported both to hold runoff and to accelerate erosion. Staggered earth bunds (tabia) in Morocco store the runoff of all rains below 50 mm on the field [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1]. In Algeria, a poorly maintained banquette becomes a factor accelerating erosion, because the smallest unrepaired breach triggers a chain reaction through the whole network in torrential and prolonged rains [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2].
conditionality: Two conditions separate the sides in the sources. Maintenance: the acceleration is tied explicitly to unrepaired breaches in state-built banquettes [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2]. Storm size: the tabia hold runoff only up to rains of 50 mm, and in bigger storms the excess overtops them and gullies the whole slope [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1]. The actionable reading is to plan and fund upkeep and spillways, not only construction. Elsewhere banquettes simply did not stop gullying: gullied areas on Tunisian banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, and over 1947-1968 Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of the Oued Fodda dam [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. Neither side is measured on plots: the protective statement is from an expert manual and the harmful ones are secondary citations within a national evaluation, and the two concern different structures, tabia and banquettes [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2].

effect_mechanism: In semi-arid catchments check dams on China's Loess Plateau are credited with cutting regional sediment export by about 85% and accounted for 37.2% to 72.2% of sediment reduction at the outlets of five catchments over 26 years, and loose-rock check dams on semi-arid USA rangeland retained 48.4% and 82.4% of watershed sediment yield [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_4, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1].
conditionality: The USA check dams produced a twofold decline in outlet sediment per unit of peak runoff, but this was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]. Sediment retention is a component proxy for water quality, the Chinese figures are secondary citations in reviews, and the USA site is high-income rangeland rather than smallholder farmland [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1].

effect_mechanism: Storage and recharge structures ease water stress in semi-arid areas: production cisterns in semi-arid Brazil keep livestock watered while clay tanks are dry, an agency review credits consumption and production cisterns with a large drop in rural establishments without any water source, and subsurface dams raise water levels in existing wells used when other sources dry up [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1]. In the field, pits and furrows keep rain in the root zone: in Burkina Faso zaï of 30–40 cm diameter and 1-m half-moons retained moisture for 2-3 weeks through dry spells, and zaï can retain moisture in the soil for seven to ten days after rainfall; in semi-arid Brazil tied furrows kept more soil moisture than the traditional flat system at all crop stages and depths [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8, ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9].
conditionality: Supply is bounded by storage: 57% of Kenyan sand dams would hold 4 months of water for their reported beneficiaries [ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1]. The Brazilian units are implementer or agency assessments, interviews or census inference from an upper-middle-income context rather than the low-income target [ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5]. Well-level evidence for semi-arid bunds and zaï now sits in the catchment water yield rows. What upstream capture does to water downstream is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows. The zaï and half-moon results come with compost in the pits, so the moisture gain cannot be credited to the pit alone [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8]. In the Brazilian trial deep ploughing, which is tillage alone and not a capture structure, scored as high as the tied furrows, and the trial ran a single season at a station of the agency that promotes the technology [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9].

effect_mechanism: Watershed treatment reduces reliance on outside supply: participating villages in India saw reduced water transportation by tanker compared with nonparticipating villages [ev_water_access_deficit_verm19_1], and an agency review credits consumption and production cisterns in semi-arid Brazil with a significant contribution to wider access to water [ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1]. In India, discharge of springs and streams rose in treated watersheds: a sample study in Himachal Pradesh reports a 40 percent increase in water discharge in spring and stream sources [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1], and the Uttarakhand project achieved an average 21 percent increase in water discharge from perennial water sources in sampled micro-watersheds, against a target of 25 percent [ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. Measured soil moisture adds a field route: a meta-analysis of in-situ practices finds they improve soil moisture retention by 59%, with soil/stone bunds at an SMD of 76.4% [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_1, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_3]; in Burkina Faso zaï of 30–40 cm diameter and 1-m half-moons retained moisture for 2-3 weeks through dry spells [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]; and Indian project watersheds showed an increase in soil moisture content by 30.5 percent compared to the IWMP sites [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2]. Water productivity, the grain produced per unit of rain, is a route by which capture eases water stress. The water-productivity evidence points the same way: FAO compilers list improved water use efficiency among the main benefits of rainwater harvesting, the WOCAT guideline authors find that all water harvesting groups indicate improved water use efficiency, mostly high to medium, through reduced evaporation loss and better soil water availability, and a review sentence, citing earlier work, says capture approaches often lead also to higher water productivity because denser canopies shade the soil [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1].
conditionality: The tanker reduction is a reported programme assessment [ev_water_access_deficit_verm19_1], and the Brazilian unit is an agency inference from census figures in an upper-middle-income context [ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1]. The Indian spring and stream discharge figures come from World Bank completion reports, the lender's own evaluation, measured before and after without untreated comparison sites, for catchment treatment that bundles plantations, trenches, ponds and check dams with water-harvesting structures, so the gain cannot be credited to water harvesting alone [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1, ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. Groundwater-recharge evidence, with its limits, now sits in the catchment water yield rows, which also answer what upstream capture does to water downstream. The pooled 59% covers mixed in-situ practices, and the zaï and half-moon result comes with compost in the pits, so neither credits a single structure [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. The Indian soil-moisture comparison is a project-commissioned study of a package of soil and water conservation structures [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2]. These are compiler and author judgements across groups, direction only, and the review sentence is second-hand; the WOCAT authors also note that some case studies indicate little to no improvement in water use efficiency [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1].
